name: Hōkūleʻa design study
summary: Herb Kāne and Kenneth Emory chose canoe features recorded across the Pacific as their best guess at ancient voyaging-canoe design for building Hōkūleʻa.
description: Kāne and Emory selected widely recorded canoe features as a hypothesis about earlier forms for an experimental vessel.
tier_reason: A particular reconstruction design hypothesis is fine detail; retain it as a testable hypothesis rather than a whole tradition. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: No ancient voyaging canoe survived, so the designers of an experimental vessel had to infer a plausible form from features recorded across many island groups.
